subject: Telemetry & privacy follow-up: SOC 2, GDPR/HIPAA notes, vendor Q kickoff

Subject: Post-demo notes: telemetry, privacy, next steps on security items

Jane — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we keep momentum while you run the internal security review:

1) SOC 2 status: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type II for our hosted API controls in Dec 2025. We have a one-page summary attached (rdw-soc2-summary) and can share the full report under NDA if needed.

2) GDPR / HIPAA: Our platform supports customer-controlled data residency and has contractual Addendum options for HIPAA BAA. For GDPR, we offer data processing addenda and detailed documentation on data handling in the console and during inference.

3) Telemetry & cookies: You asked where telemetry comes from and what is collected. Short answer: the console collects operational telemetry (request latencies, error rates, token counts) and anonymous usage metrics for product health. No PII is logged by default in telemetry; developers can enable more detailed request logging for troubleshooting (opt-in per project). Docs link: https://console.redwood.ai/docs/privacy#telemetry (attached one-pager).

4) Vendor questionnaire: Marcus mentioned wanting a kickoff on the vendor security questionnaire (VSQ). If you can send the spreadsheet/questions now we’ll populate the answers and return a marked-up copy.

Next steps (proposed):
- Marcus: please send the VSQ file to security@redwood.ai and cc me (we can also accept the spreadsheet attached).
- Jane: flag any high-priority controls (encryption at rest, key management, audit log retention) we should answer first.
- Internal: I’ll loop in dev for console telemetry specifics and a short inventory of what we consider operational telemetry vs request payload retention.

I attached a short one-pager on privacy and telemetry and a blank copy of the VSQ to accelerate.

Thanks — Marissa

Marissa / Ben — noted. Draft answers below (quick bullets) and attached telemetry matrix for Acme to review. If you want the polished text for the spreadsheet I’ll format it, but this covers the content:

- Request payloads / retraining: DEFAULT: no customer data is used to train public models. Customers may opt-in to a private feedback program where sanitized examples are used under contract; otherwise all customer input is treated as ephemeral telemetry for platform health only.

- Log retention & residency: Console operational logs (latency/error/metrics) retained by default 90 days in the region of deployment (US: us-central-1). Audit logs (access events) retained 365 days by default with export to S3/GCS available. We can extend retention or provide archival exports per contract.

- Docs site cookies / third-party trackers: docs.redwood.ai serves minimal analytics. We use a first-party telemetry endpoint for documentation usage and a non-identifying Google Analytics property filtered to exclude user identifiers. No third-party script has access to request payloads. We can provide a cookie inventory.

Attached: telemetry-matrix.xlsx (maps telemetry types -> retention -> owner). I can convert bullets above into the VSQ cells and return the annotated spreadsheet when you send it.

Thanks — Dev
